outcome: Help providers and payers assemble complete evidence, resolve claims, and explain exceptions faster under authorised review.
overview: Revenue-cycle teams rebuild the same claim evidence by hand, payer rules change faster than the checklists that encode them, and denials arrive weeks after the care was delivered. This solution assembles claim evidence from approved clinical, coding and billing sources, checks it against versioned payer contracts and policies with deterministic rules, and shows exactly which support is missing rather than filling the gap. Coders and medical reviewers approve every submission and appeal, each carrying its citations and reason. An 8–12-week proof of value targets a 30% reduction in selected clean-claim handling time, fewer avoidable denials, and an auditable reason behind every recommendation.

benefits.text: Reduce selected clean-claim handling time by a target 30%
benefits.limits: Basis: hypothesis. Target to validate against the customer’s own claim-workflow baseline during the proof of value — not a guarantee

benefits.text: Reduce avoidable denials and rework through evidence completeness checks before submission
benefits.limits: Basis: hypothesis. Denial movement depends on payer behaviour and contract terms; no acceptance or reimbursement outcome is guaranteed, and results are measured against a finance-confirmed baseline

benefits.text: Provide a citation, a rule version and an auditable reason for 100% of recommendations and appeals
benefits.source: Reference architecture citation and versioning design, Redington Healthcare catalogue,
benefits.limits: A design property of the evidence and rule-versioning workflow, verified in UAT and appeal sampling; not a claim about payer acceptance

residency: Deployable in-country on local AWS or Azure regions (e.g. UAE, KSA); clinical, coding and claims data stay in the customer tenancy in the reference designs, in line with UAE and Saudi health-data regulations and national claims-platform rules

notFor.situation: Payer contracts and policies are not available in a maintainable, versioned form
notFor.why: Deterministic checking depends on knowing which rule version applied on the date of service; unversioned policy makes every finding unappealable

notFor.situation: Expectation of guaranteed payer acceptance, reimbursement uplift or automated up-coding
notFor.why: The source catalogue is explicit that no payer acceptance or reimbursement is guaranteed; coding must follow documented clinical evidence, and anything else is a compliance exposure rather than a benefit

notFor.situation: No clinical documentation depth behind the claim lines being submitted
notFor.why: The solution shows missing support rather than inventing it, so a thin record yields flagged gaps and no acceleration

scope:
Model: Joint delivery: accredited implementation partner leads, with Redington architecture and commercial governance; the customer owns coding policy, medical-necessity decisions and the compliance position · Duration: 8–12-week proof of value; 16–28 weeks to scaled deployment
Delivery pod: Partner delivery lead + project manager, integration engineer, revenue-cycle analyst, data engineer; customer revenue-cycle director, coding lead, medical reviewer, compliance officer, EHR and claims-system integration leads, privacy and security approvers · Support model: Business-hours or 24×7 option; severity-based response targets; partner service desk with vendor escalation
1) Denial diagnostic and finance-confirmed baseline
2) Contract and policy ingestion with version governance
3) EHR, coding, billing and exchange integration
4) Rule calibration on a blinded claim benchmark with coding and compliance review
5) Controlled proof of value with weekly financial and quality review
6) Stabilisation, finance-confirmed benefit review and handover
deliverables: Evidence and coding quality meet the agreed thresholds on the blinded claim benchmark
Every finding records the contract and policy version applied on the date of service
100% of submissions and appeals show coder and, where required, medical-review approval
Claims exchange reconciles with the payer or national platform, including denial and appeal states
Security and privacy tests passed; an appeal sample is reviewed and finance confirms the baseline
